reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin as a business opportunity and urges viewers to sign up or buy paid education packages connected to token production. It uses projected gains of 55 to 110 times, future coin values, urgency, and bonus claims to encourage immediate purchases, although the visible chart characterizes the values as predictions rather than established outcomes.

opening.argument: The presentation does not state that its price targets are certain: the chart expressly calls them predictions and says whether they are reached depends on members’ commitment and effort. The speaker also tells viewers to educate themselves about cryptocurrency. That leaves room to read the figures as conditional market commentary, however optimistic, rather than a promised return. The case for treating the projections as guarantees is weakened by the video’s own qualification of them.

citations.quote: yourself and make yourself aware of the powerful benefits of Cryptocurrency

rebuttal.rebuttal: The purchase language and package table show an offer, but they do not erase the distinction between a forecast and a guarantee. The chart labels its scenarios as predictions and makes the outcome conditional; the spoken figures likewise describe goals. A forceful forecast may warrant skepticism, but this evidence alone does not establish that the speaker represented appreciation as certain.

citations.quote: our company shows that within the next 36 months their goal is to bring the value of the coin up to somewhere between $55 and 110 US dollars.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The caveat qualifies the chart; it does not change the sales pitch surrounding it. The speaker turns the proposed future prices into dramatic profit calculations and then urges immediate package acquisition to participate in the claimed growth. A conditional label cannot by itself establish that the underlying valuation or projected returns are sound.

opening.argument: The video spends substantial time explaining cryptocurrency, comparing Bitcoin’s history with OneCoin, describing an educational offering, and showing how tokens are said to produce coins. The speaker describes the academy’s subjects as cryptocurrency basics, benefits, trading, and the industry’s future. Its central format can therefore be read as an educational presentation about a proposed cryptocurrency system, even though it also promotes packages; the presence of a sales pitch does not make every explanation itself a scam mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening identifies paid packages and an immediate buying instruction, but that does not establish that the video’s explanation is merely a deceptive solicitation. It also describes what the academy is said to teach and how its token mechanism is presented. The growth chart calls its values predictions, not achieved outcomes. Those details support treating this as an educational pitch about a speculative product, rather than proof that the educational framing is false.

citations.quote: Now depending on which package you buy, that will determine what level of access you get to how far your academy will go to our Online Education

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational material is bundled with paid access and tokens the speaker says can produce coins, and the video explicitly converts projected prices into prospective profits before calling for immediate purchase. Explaining a product does not make that product’s investment claims reliable; the chart’s prediction disclaimer confirms the gains are not established outcomes.

citations.quote: you can use these tokens tokens here in these packages to actually produce cryptocurrency coins, which puts money right back into your pocket.
So get your package immediately and start mining your coins so that you can participate in this growth.

opening.argument: What is visibly offered is a tiered package with stated prices and different levels of online academy access, alongside tokens and gold coins. The speaker says the tokens are used to produce cryptocurrency coins and emphasizes that participation need not depend on recruiting others. The supplied material does not show a credential request, an explicit guaranteed return, or downline-based compensation. Those limits matter: a strongly promotional, speculative package offer is not by itself evidence of those particular scam mechanisms.

citations.quote: our packages also come with free gold coins and they will come also with a certain amount of tokens
This is, finally, a business model that can truly reward you significantly potentially creating great wealth in your life legitimately without having to recruit anyone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The listed prices, package contents, and education access are concrete features of a service offer. The reference opening’s emphasis on projected gains and urgency shows aggressive promotion, but the values are identified as predictions and the speaker describes the package as access to education plus tokens. The supplied evidence does not show that a buyer must recruit others or that a return is guaranteed.

citations.quote: without having to recruit anyone.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ordinary package framing does not neutralize what the package is sold to do: the speaker says tokens produce coins and money back into the buyer’s pocket, then illustrates large prospective gains and presses viewers to buy now. The absence of a shown credential request or recruitment requirement does not resolve whether the token-linked investment claims are misleading.
